agree: The pain is real and costly: payout delays coincide with loans, card debt, cut ad spend and postponed inventory.
Adjacent spending is proven: brands pay for finance software, bookkeeping, financing and human forecasting.
A one-off plan is a plausible wedge: human-built forecasts appear mainly in retainers or a $6,000-$10,000 project.
Spreadsheet delivery fits current behavior: owners already use sheets, payout reports and accounting tools.
disagree: Demand is not confirmed: zero threads requested a forecast service; coping with debt proves pain, not willingness to pay $750.
The price is untested: $750 is cheaper than listed human alternatives, but no buyer compared or bought this exact scope.
The $1,250 monthly update is premature: it approaches fractional-CFO pricing without a defined ongoing outcome or retention evidence.
Faceless delivery weakens the trust case: borrowing and cash recommendations need a named, credible accountable expert; show the owner's background.
Fifteen notes test outreach, not demand: measure calls, alternatives, objections and paid commitments rather than treating replies as validation.
missing: Segment validation: the $3M-plus, Amazon-heavy target and big-order trigger are assumptions; check who feels this pain most acutely.
Delivery economics: no estimate of data-cleaning, modeling and revision time, so $750 profitability is unknown.
Accuracy and accountability: required source data, assumptions, error handling and limits on borrowing advice are unspecified.
Competitive switching test: no direct comparison against Drivepoint, an accountant, a spreadsheet or simply borrowing earlier.
top_three: Sell the exact $750 plan to owners with an imminent order; require payment before custom work and record every objection.
Interview recent order decisions to establish current spend, spreadsheet effort, financing cost and why existing advisers or tools did not solve timing.
Run a named-expert pilot with credentials, a sample output and clear accuracy and advice boundaries; remove the monthly offer until repeat demand appears.
